correctness.rationale: For the explicit deterministic-order-two tableau b1=1-b, b2=b, a21=1/(2b), the exact scalar multiplier is R=1-z[(1-b)Y1+bY2]+z^2Y1Y2/2. Independence yields Q_b=1-2z+[1+a-2(a-1)b(1-b)]z^2-az^3+a^2z^4/4. Subtracting b=1/2 gives 2(a-1)(b-1/2)^2z^2. Orthogonal diagonalization and iteration independence prove the arbitrary SPD and finite-horizon moments. The cubic after factoring Q_b-1 by z/4 has derivative minimum 4C-16/3>=8/3, hence a unique positive stability boundary. Midpoint factors at 2/a; implicit differentiation of the Heun root gives a strictly increasing normalized horizon and high-noise ratio 2. Reusing Y at both stages creates a degree-four polynomial, proving the fourth-moment obstruction; a scaled Pareto(3) distribution verifies the strict separation. The actual packaged standalone standard-library verifier was run successfully on 162 rational two-stage samples, 162 exact gap identities, 108 rotated-SPD tests, 63 frontier cases, and the Pareto witness. Numerical checks are supplementary to the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 stochastic Runge–Kutta–Chebyshev primary preprint uses a common sampled batch at its internal stages and supplies general convergence and deterministic RKC stability discussion, not the stated independently sampled two-stage order-two tableau optimum. The 2023 exact SGD stability paper concerns one gradient query per iteration. Earlier stochastic-Heun SDE literature uses Stratonovich Brownian increments rather than stage-resampled empirical gradient multipliers. The closest mathematical records cover other algorithms and do not imply the exact tableau-wide noise penalty, universal cubic, or second-versus-fourth moment distinction. No covering statement was identified, though specialist publication priority remains unverified.
residual_risks: An older or poorly indexed investigation of independently resampled Runge–Kutta gradient stages may have derived an equivalent tableau identity.
The 2011 Japanese-language Heun SDE work was inspected at method-defining pages but not translated in full; its different model is clear from the displayed stochastic equation.
No claim is made that search coverage certifies publication priority; independent specialist verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: Deterministic RK2 stability on a linear quadratic cannot distinguish tableau coefficients, yet independent stage noise selects the equal-weight tableau uniquely over every SPD matrix and every horizon. The exact stability ceiling gives a parameter- and noise-aware step guarantee; its improvement over the midpoint/SGD ceiling rises strictly to a factor two. A Pareto(3) oracle makes the seemingly innocuous choice of reusing a batch change a contracting finite mean-square iteration into infinite one-step variance. Together these are structural design distinctions for stochastic multi-stage gradient evaluations, not a generic textbook stability-polynomial calculation. The claim is confined to a motivating interpolation quadratic and does not assert cost-normalized superiority.
